wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. For purpose=agent_control the immutable accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision is resolved by its whole-value claim of retype(this EventId, realm); the genesis MUST NOT carry a backward agent_provision ref, which would create an EventId cycle. The verifier cross-binds the complete actor/controller AccountIds, PCR delegation and provision payload before materializing Agent status. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch proves its separate accepted organization authority. A self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact account ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the root-round responder; glare branch: the full signed request Event author ActorId referenced by requests[0], never the Station receipt issuer_id; requests MUST be strictly ascending by the complete request_event_ref wire string UTF-8 unsigned bytes, with duplicate Event refs rejected regardless of receipt digest and no receiver-side sorting or deduplication), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.sidecar_account_self_authored_proof: Admitted only when Event actor_id is the account branch and its complete AccountId is the authenticated controller account. The reducer derives controller_account_id byte-for-byte from actor_id.account_id, uses (realm_id, controller_account_id) as the singleton key, and rejects the service actor branch with sidecar_create_denied before revealing existence. The same exact AccountId binds Sidecar membership, MLS genesis and participant authority; principal-only equality is forbidden.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry and resolve to exactly one closed payload schema.
An accepted durable Event becomes shared history only when the current authority includes its exact bytes in a signed RealmCommit for the Event's own Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream.
Stream identity is derived from the Event's closed scope. Realm, each Circle, and each Sidecar have independent commit streams; no Realm-global total chain exists.
Event carries no chain predecessor or authority-commit proof. Only RealmCommit carries previous_commit_ref, and only within the same stream.
Reducers derive typed current results by replaying committed Events in stream position order. Account-private material is outside shared authority-commit streams.

result_writes[] is the machine contract for which typed current results one Event kind writes, in what order, and under which closed condition; zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 10 read it as the source of truth, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_contracts validates every declared row: a declared value_projection member MUST be declared by that row's value_schema_ref, and a whole-value set MUST write every member that schema requires. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND THIS IS A KNOWN GAP: 73 of the 139 reducer_input kinds declare it; the remaining 66 still have no machine-readable reducer contract, so their registered writes exist only in prose. The declaring kinds are deliberately not enumerated here: event_kinds[] already is that list, the enumeration that used to sit in this sentence went stale behind it, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_coverage_note now recomputes both counts from the rows and fails when this sentence disagrees. Normative prose MUST NOT cite result_writes[] for a kind that does not declare it -- a citation without a row is the exact defect this array was added to close. The converse obligation binds a declaring kind: a kind's rows MUST enumerate EVERY typed current result its accepted admission writes on the shared face, so a kind that writes four families and declares one describes itself wrongly in the artifact readers are told is the source of truth. That obligation cannot be gated here, because the lint has no second list of a kind's writes to compare a row set against; it is normative in zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1 and it is why a kind with atomic multi-family writes lands all of them in one batch or none. Extend coverage kind by kind and shrink this note; do not narrow the rule to make it read as complete.

transition_contracts declares the lifecycle axis of a typed current result family: its closed state set, its entry idiom (exactly one of initial_state / initial_states / template), its terminal states and its allowed (from, to) edges. tools/artifact_lint:fsm_reachability reads it together with every transition result_projection and requires that each declared state be reachable from the entry set, that each allowed edge have a write that can perform it, that no const edge leave the table and that no terminal state carry an outgoing edge. A family that declares a machine MUST NOT be written by any non-transition projection: a set installs a state without passing the table, which would make allowed_transitions documentation rather than a rule. Between the authority-commit clean break and 2026-09-18 this block did not exist while the gate still read it under the removed cell_* names, so check reported success over four normative paragraphs (zh/models/circle.md, zh/models/morph.md, zh/models/realm-and-space.md, zh/models/strand-and-message.md) that name transition_contracts as the source of truth for object lifecycle transitions; an absent or empty block is now a failure. Those four object families are themselves still unregistered, so their archive / restore lifecycle has no machine contract yet -- that is a coverage gap, not a licence to read the prose as satisfied.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

result_writes.notes: One of the FOUR typed current results one accepted ak.agent.provision writes in a single reducer transaction; identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3 forbids exposing a partially completed state, so any required write failing rolls the whole set back. The provisioning fact itself, keyed by the Agent DID alone. It is deliberately NOT keyed by the Agent's full account ActorId: models/actor.md derives that ActorId from payload.agent_id plus this Event's exact controller account and Station and only reconciles it against genesis.actor_id after genesis, and this Event's own envelope actor_id is the CONTROLLER, so an ActorId subject would be unconstructible here. The line in section 3.6 that forbids a bare DidCoreId subject governs the LIFECYCLE family, whose reason -- one principal on two Stations is two accounts -- is discharged in this family by the Realm component plus the same-Station rule of section 3.6.3. Every member is a plain signed-payload copy; requested_scope itself stays controller-private and only its digest is projected. A second provision declaring an agent_id an accepted provision already carries MUST be rejected with zero writes (agent_provisioning_already_declared) -- that rejection is admission semantics, not pre_state_requirements[], because every registered predicate is positive over a stored field and "no row for this subject" has no spelling.

The scope component is digested and the stored member goes through normalized_string_set for the same reason the standalone writer does it: this payload's const is a bare string and the standalone payload MAY carry a one-element array, and both have to reach the same subject and the same stored value. not_before is envelope.created_at, which is safe to read here only because an admission check requires payload.created_at to equal it byte-for-byte -- two signed times MUST NOT disagree. grant_status is the literal active. expires_at is NOT projected: section 3.3.1 makes absence mean non-expiring and forbids both a JSON null and the server's receive time. source_event_ref and the inner proof are likewise absent -- the head Event and its acceptance proof carry provenance, and copying an event_id into the value would make two semantically identical endorsements unequal.

One of the FOUR typed current results one accepted ak.agent.provision writes in a single reducer transaction; identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3 forbids exposing a partially completed state, so any required write failing rolls the whole set back. This writer has NO inner selector proof and MUST NOT be dressed up as a signed claim: a portable response that has to return selector_claim.proofs needs the real controller-signed claim, and a service MUST NOT counter-sign or expose private provision material to fill the DTO. subject_account_id comes from the registered derivation agent_account_id_from_provision -- principal from the signed payload.agent_id, station from this Event's own envelope.actor_id -- because select picks one field path and nothing in this grammar joins a payload principal to an envelope station; the value is still fully determinate on the wire. audience is projected only when the payload carries selector_audience, which its own schema makes conditional on selector_visibility being restricted. They resolve the Agent here and then read the remaining create-locked members from agent_provisioning keyed by it, so no member of the create-locked four-tuple lives in two families. Strand business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at; ak.strand.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Strand's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=strand_already_terminal; state=archived yields strand_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. v1 has no per-Realm workflow profile carrier: these hard invariants are the complete transition rule and receivers MUST NOT narrow admission from Realm-private configuration (zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.4).

Set or clear a per-(strand, actor) watch subscription. Writes a current-value projection typed current result keyed by (strand_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST be paired with a same-batch ak.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others; the audit event carries refs[role=audit_pair] plus the suite-bearing paired_event_id pointing at the write, and derives its digest from that ID. The write MUST NOT reference the audit event (encoding.md 6.0.1 forbids mutual preimages). The watches Relation (actor --watches--> strand) is a derived projection of this typed current result, not a separate truth source — direct ak.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. result_writes.notes: models/views.md section 3.2 table row 1. The selector carries no field because ak.view.create is id_source=event_derived: the View id IS this Event own event_id retyped, so naming a payload field would claim a second, forgeable source. payload.object is the closed author definition -- the same region ak.view.reconcile replaces -- and NOT the materialized object: everything the author does not define is produced here by the registered create-lock derivations of common-fields.md section 3.3. result_writes.notes: models/views.md section 3.2 table row 3 and the normative paragraph under it: reconcile is neither create object snapshot nor update patch, it replaces the definition wholesale, and it writes the SAME family as the other two kinds -- definition is the complete author-editable View definition, not a second business object. payload.definition is view.schema.json#/$defs/view_definition rather than the materialized object: a materialized schema used as an authoring input reopens exactly the ownership the patch surface protects. The reducer composes the accepted definition with the retained members and the derived update metadata and validates the complete result against the materialized schema. state is retained, so reconcile can neither tombstone nor resurrect; it MUST reject a tombstoned target with failed_precondition reason_code=view_already_terminal and MUST NOT carry an id.

result_writes.notes: models/views.md section 3.2 table row 2, and the one write section 3.1 makes normatively load-bearing: a shared View has no tombstone event kind, so its protocol-level removal IS this patch setting state=tombstoned. allowed_paths is not a new enumeration -- it is the complement the reducer-managed-path-registry already fixed: the 21 declared View members minus the effective forbidden set for this object, with `state` subtracted by the single registered universal exemption. The registry is read per object, so another family declaring `stage` or `resolution` cannot narrow this set and this exemption cannot widen theirs. state_changed_at stays reducer-derived and conditional: only an accepted active -> tombstoned transition produces it, an author-supplied value MUST be rejected, and a terminal View MUST fail any later update or reconcile with failed_precondition reason_code=view_already_terminal. The four retained members are the create-locked identity and creation metadata, preserved verbatim from the frozen pre-state; a patch MUST NOT reach them and this write MUST NOT re-derive them.
